headline: Council approved $735,000 in opioid funds for a winter warming shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway; emergency declaration at 654 Riverside Street failed.
summary: The council approved the Northeast Air lease extension, a Lancaster Street parking change, and new parking fees for First Light Commons lots. It approved $735,000 from the opioid settlement fund for a warming shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway and postponed a $350,000 version. An emergency declaration for a shelter at 654 Riverside Street failed.
decisions: Approved raising the Portland Development Corporation business assistance grant from $10,000 to $20,000, unanimously.
The motion to postpone the 54 Danforth Street license to November 16 failed.
Approved the catering and combined entertainment license at 54 Danforth Street, unanimously.
Approved the Class 1 license application at 476 Stevens, unanimously.
Approved changing Lancaster Street to a one-hour parking zone and allowing Portland High School students to park there, unanimously.
Approved new parking fees for the First Light Commons lots, unanimously.
Approved a 20-year extension of the Northeast Air ground lease, conditioned on replacing the hangar with at least a $4 million investment, unanimously.
Approved the purchase and sale agreement between Nordic main LLC and Portland for Portland Technology Park units 3 and 5, unanimously.
Approved a salary increase for Corporation Council, unanimously.
The motion to declare a limited emergency at 654 Riverside Street failed, 4 to 5.
Approved $735,000 from the opioid settlement fund for the warming shelter at 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway, after an amendment lowered the request from $900,000, 8 to 1.
Postponed indefinitely the $350,000 opioid fund order for the winter warming shelter.
discussion: 54 Danforth Street license: Neighbors said doors were left open and music was loud, and the operator said a staff member would now monitor noise. Members debated postponing the license for more review or granting it now with conditions.

Winter warming shelter funding: Speakers urged that opioid settlement funds go to treatment and recovery, while members noted staff had found the funds allowed for shelter use. Members debated whether the Homeless Services Center or 166 Riverside Industrial Parkway should host the shelter.

Shelter access for trespassed people: Members asked whether people with criminal trespass orders could use the Homeless Services Center shelter. Staff said they could not, and the city may have no other place for them on some nights.
CMP transmission corridor upgrades: A public speaker asked for an independent review of the proposed upgrades. The speaker said most outages start on local lines, not transmission lines.
Creative Portland: The committee postponed a Creative Portland item after residents raised concerns. Councilors said next steps would include meetings with the board and would move slowly.
